stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. There exists a closed
subscheme $Z \subset Y$ such that $f$ factors through $Z$ and such
that for any other closed subscheme $Z' \subset Y$ such that $f$
factors through $Z'$ we have $Z \subset Z'$.
hypotheses: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
conclusions:

subscheme $Z \subset Y$ such that $f$ factors through $Z$ and such
that for any other closed subscheme $Z' \subset Y$ such that $f$
factors through $Z'$ we have $Z \subset Z'$.

reason: The ideal Ker(O_Y→f_*O_X) has a maximal quasi-coherent sub-ideal, defining the smallest closed subscheme of Y through which f factors.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X_1 \ar[d] \ar[r]_{f_1} & Y_1 \ar[d] \\
X_2 \ar[r]^{f_2} & Y_2
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of schemes. Let $Z_i \subset Y_i$, $i = 1, 2$ be
the scheme theoretic image of $f_i$. Then the morphism
$Y_1 \to Y_2$ induces a morphism $Z_1 \to Z_2$ and a
commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X_1 \ar[r] \ar[d] & Z_1 \ar[d] \ar[r] & Y_1 \ar[d] \\
X_2 \ar[r] & Z_2 \ar[r] & Y_2
}
$$

X_2 \ar[r]^{f_2} & Y_2

$$
be a commutative diagram of schemes. Let $Z_i \subset Y_i$, $i = 1, 2$ be
the scheme theoretic image of $f_i$.
conclusions:
the morphism
$Y_1 \to Y_2$ induces a morphism $Z_1 \to Z_2$ and a
commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X_1 \ar[r] \ar[d] & Z_1 \ar[d] \ar[r] & Y_1 \ar[d] \\
X_2 \ar[r] & Z_2 \ar[r] & Y_2
}
$$

reason: Pulling back the scheme-theoretic image of f₂ along Y₁→Y₂ yields a closed subscheme through which f₁ factors; minimality gives the induced map Z₁→Z₂.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a separated morphism of schemes.
Let $V \subset Y$ be a retrocompact open. Let $s : V \to X$
be a morphism such that $f \circ s = \text{id}_V$.
Let $Y'$ be the scheme theoretic image of $s$.
Then $Y' \to Y$ is an isomorphism over $V$.
hypotheses:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a separated morphism of schemes.
Let $V \subset Y$ be a retrocompact open. Let $s : V \to X$
be a morphism such that $f \circ s = \text{id}_V$.
Let $Y'$ be the scheme theoretic image of $s$.

reason: A retrocompact section has quasi-compact scheme-theoretic image commuting with restriction to opens; over V it is the image of a section of a separated map, hence isomorphic to V.
